oneOf.description: Evaluate `needs.requires` against an explicit target profile.
Check an issue id, project key, tags, status and priority.
Whether an issue is ready or blocked, given its blockers' statuses.

Classify one delivery and answer what it needs to merge (CAD-1946).

The evidence is the caller's own reads: the project's `delivery:`
section, its recorded approval, the diff rows and the trusted-base list
texts. Nothing here reads a file or a program, and no input carries a
class.

Blocker.description:
A `blocked_by` target and its current status. A target that cannot be
found counts as open: pass any status that is not `done` or `dropped`.

Change.description:
One changed file of the PR diff — the shape `git diff --raw -z
--no-renames` emits and `scripts/enqueue-reviewed` collects.

old_mode.description: Octal mode text (`"100644"`); `"000000"` on the absent side of an add.

DeliveryApprovalInput.description:
The delivery half of a project work approval: the digest it recorded and
the policy it approved.

DeliveryPolicy.description:
A project's delivery policy — `PROJECT.md` `delivery:` or the
defaults. [`parse`] builds it through the strict raw types and
[`DeliveryPolicy::validate`]; `serde` round-trips the validated
form (the approval payload's `delivery` key).

integration_branch.description:
CAD-1561: one extra PR target beyond the repository default
branch. `None` is omitted from the canonical JSON so existing
digests and approvals are unchanged. A non-default target is
admitted only while the exact current approved policy names it —
last-approved fallbacks (`delivery_unapproved` notes) do not.

max_revise.description: REVISE verdicts a ticket takes before the operator decides.

oversized.description: Over this a delivery cannot merge through the loop.

reviews.description: The named reviews a `risk` rule may require.

risk.description:
Risk rules: a delivery must satisfy every review `require`d by
every rule whose `when` holds. A rule with no `when` always
applies.

solo_operator.description:
Optional legacy CAD-1298 profile, retained for compatible reads.
CAD-1314 needs no profile for default lean classification. Keeping
`None` omitted preserves existing canonical digests and approvals;
requirements always use [`Resolved`], never the raw file.

DeliveryRequirementsInput.description:
Input of `delivery.requirements.evaluate`.

Every field is evidence the caller retrieved itself: the project's
`delivery:` section, its recorded approval, the diff rows and the
trusted-base list texts. No field carries a class, and nothing here reads a
file, a program or a network answer.

approval.description: The project's recorded work approval, when one exists.

policy.description: The exact `delivery:` section text, or absent when the project has none.

ReadinessInput.description: Input of `issue.readiness`. `id` names the issue in the refusal.

target.description:
The host being asked. Required: there is no native, hosted or other
default profile, and a missing one is refused, never assumed.

Review.description: One named review a rule may require. `kind` picks the variant.

oneOf.description: An independent agent review; `focus` is one of [`FOCI`].

A GitHub App check (a bot). `mode: advisory` never blocks;
`required` blocks like an agent review.

require.description: Names in `reviews` the delivery must satisfy.

when.description:
The conditions under which the rule applies — ANY of them.
Absent: the rule always applies.

paths.description:
Repo-relative, file-level globs — the same grammar as the
`areas:` reader and `paths=` ([`crate::delivery_rules::check_path`]):
`*` and `?` match inside one segment, a `**` segment any number,
a trailing `/` everything under it. Slice 3 matches them with
`areas::matches`, so the two grammars must agree.

SoloOperatorProfile.description:
The legacy solo-operator delivery profile (CAD-1298), still readable
after CAD-1314 made the tiers default for valid default-equivalent policies.
Custom, malformed and unapproved policies retain strict requirements.
`version` is forward-proofing:
`1` is the only accepted value, an unknown one refuses the whole
section, so an older binary never silently accepts a profile shape it
does not understand.

TargetContract.description: One contract a target provides, with the stage it is actually at.

majors.description: The contract majors this target serves, 1 to 8 values in 1..=99.

stage.description: What the target actually does with the contract — never more.

TargetProfile.description:
A host's own capability profile, supplied by the caller. This crate never
substitutes the native registry ([`crate::app_compat::SUPPORTED_CONTRACTS`])
for it: native deliberately provides a different contract set (for example
it does not serve `app-storage`), so copying it would answer for the wrong
host. Contract names are host-owned data here, not entries in this build's
registry — a target that really serves a contract may name it.

contracts.description:
Every host contract the target provides. An explicit empty map is a
host that provides none; omitting the field is an absent profile and
refuses.

core.description:
The running *host's* version: an exact semantic version. This is the
platform the package would run on, never the rules-core/wasm release
that computes the answer — those are different versions, and a caller
that cannot prove the host's own version must refuse rather than send
the rules version.

TargetStage.description:
The stage a target declares for a contract. Closed set: an unknown stage
is a profile this core cannot evaluate and refuses.

oneOf.description: A strict validator exists; nothing executes the declaration.
A consumer renders or runs the descriptor in a sandbox.

ValidateInput.description: Input of `issue.validate`: every field is optional and checked when set.
